PP1 · Chapter 4 of 6

Which ones belong?

Sort familiar things by one visible rule before combining clues.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Meet the shapes. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can find things that belong together.
  • I can find the one that is different.
  • I can count just one group.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 3

Sort by colour

The apple and the red block are red.

The ball and the blue block are blue.

We put red with red, blue with blue.

Screen 2 of 3

The odd one out

Three of these are balls.

One is a star.

The star is different. It is the odd one out.

Screen 3 of 3

Count one group

Some counters are orange. Some are blue.

Count only the orange ones.

There are 4 orange counters.

Words to know
sort
Put things that are alike in the same place.
same
Alike in one way, like colour.
different
Not like the others. The odd one out.

For parents

What your child learns

Your child sorts things by one clear rule, such as colour, and finds the one that is different. Sorting is the start of data and logic.

A common slip

Mixing two rules at once, like colour and shape. Pick one rule, say it aloud, then sort.

5-minute home activity: Sock and toy sort

  1. Pile a few socks or toys on the floor.
  2. Say one rule, like "Sort by colour".
  3. Let your child make the groups. Ask, "Which group has more?"
  4. Hide one odd item in a group. Ask your child to find it.
